files.CLAUDE.md:
# Tide table

A small shell tool that reads a harbour's tide readings from a text file and
prints the high and low water times for each day.

## Layout

- `tides.sh` is the entry script. It reads one readings file and prints a table.
- `check.sh` runs the script on the sample file and diffs the output.
- `data/harbour-sample.txt` is a short readings file for quick checks.
- `data/expected-sample.txt` is the output the sample should produce.
- `data/readings-march.txt` is a longer month of readings from the quay sensor.
- `README.md` holds usage notes for the harbour office.

## Commands

- `sh tides.sh data/harbour-sample.txt` prints the table for the sample.
- `sh check.sh` compares the script's output with the expected file.
- `grep -c . data/readings-march.txt` counts the lines in the March file.

## Conventions

- One reading per line: date, time and height in metres, split by single spaces.
- Dates are written year-month-day and times use a 24 hour clock.
- The script is POSIX shell plus awk and needs nothing else installed.
- Keep shell functions short and comment anything that depends on the file layout.
- Output is plain text, one block per day, high water listed before low water.
- Error messages go to standard error and the script exits with status 2.

## Working style

- Keep each change small enough to read in one sitting.
- Run `sh check.sh` and quote its last line when you finish.
- Ask first if a change needs a new directory.
files.README.md:
# Tide table

Usage: `sh tides.sh READINGS_FILE`

The readings file has one line per reading: a date, a time and a height in
metres. The script groups the lines by day and prints the highest and lowest
reading of each day together with the time it happened.

Sample files live in `data/`. Staff at the harbour office print the output and
pin it to the notice board by the slipway.

turns: Read tides.sh and README.md and tell me in a few lines how the script groups readings by day. After that, list what is under data/. In my own notes I call this working branch LANTERNSKIFF.

Add a --station option to tides.sh so a readings line can start with a four-letter station code before the date. Print every time as the harbour's local time and never convert to UTC, since the printed boards on the quay are all in local time.

Use grep to find every line in data/readings-march.txt that has two question marks, and quote the first match back to me word for word. No action needed on the harbour office meeting, it moved to Thursday afternoon.
Put the new station handling in a separate file called station.sh and source it from tides.sh. Nothing else should move.

Make the output show heights rounded to one decimal. check.sh diffs text exactly, so a second decimal makes the comparison fail. A while back I tried a sort pipeline for the grouping and put it back, no action needed there.

I have changed my mind about the order of days: list them newest first instead, since staff mostly look up this week. Earlier I had asked for oldest first, so flip the order in the awk block and in check.sh.

Here is the plan for the rest of the week, in sequence: skip the dropout markers in the maths, then add a station test to check.sh, then write a usage section in the README. Only write that plan into your notes, nothing to build yet.
Add a line to the README about the quay sensor. Its clock runs five minutes fast, so subtract five minutes before comparing readings with the printed boards.
